title: Multiplex Cyclical Immunofluorescence on Fresh Frozen Tissue
author: Maya Brewer
materials: frozen slides
formalin
1X Universal Blocking Reagent (UBR)
ddH2O
Antibody Diluent Reagent
primary antibody
PBS
fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody
Hoechst 33342
glycerol
Dilute fluorophore-conjugated primary antibodies using Antibody Diluent Reagent.
Add diluted antibodies to each section and incubate overnight at 4˚C.
Sections II-IV are repeated for each remaining cycle.
To remove solutions from sections that are in the humidified chamber, tip the solution off of the slide into the chamber. Removing solutions from slides in humidified chamber.
Controls: When testing new antibodies, extra sections are used for controls to determine the autofluorescence and specificity of each antibody.

Positive control: Most antibodies used have targets that are found in kidney tissue in high amounts. For the immune cell markers used within this project, the antibodies are first tested in spleen tissue to confirm they work. They are then validated in kidney tissue.

Directly conjugated antibodies are validated in the same steps as those that are unconjugated. A secondary antibody in a different fluorophore from the direct conjugate is added to confirm the conjugation.
The working dilution for directly conjugated antibodies is determined based on the specificity, intensity (secondary vs. direct conjugate), and signal: noise ratio.

Directly conjugated antibodies are tested for the ability to withstand one freeze/thaw cycle. This is completed by freezing a small aliquot of the conjugated antibody at -20C. This aliquot is thawed and stained on a section adjacent to a section stained with an aliquot of the antibody that has not been frozen.
All antibodies conjugated in the lab are validated via quantifying the moles of dye: moles of protein (acceptable range: 0.7-2). See Antibody Purification and Labeling Protocol for details.
New lots of antibodies are validated by staining the old lot while simultaneously staining the new lot using a series of dilutions including the optimized dilution of the old lot.
The antibodies are compared to when they were previously stained alone to ensure the specificity and intensity remains the same.

steps.title: Post-fix and Wash Sections
steps.instruction: Post-fix frozen slides from the -80˚C freezer and wash them with PBS.

substeps.instruction: Place frozen slides directly into formalin and post-fix for 5 minutes.
Discard used formalin into the appropriate waste container.
Fill jar with 1X PBS and wash sections for 5 minutes, four times.

steps.title: Block Sections
steps.instruction: Apply a hydrophobic barrier and block the tissue sections.

substeps.instruction: Draw a large barrier around each section using a hydrophobic pen, ensuring the pen does not touch the section.
Dilute 10X Universal Blocking Reagent (UBR) to 1X using 9-parts ddH2O to 1-part UBR.
Block sections for 30 minutes with 1X UBR at room temperature.

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with the primary antibody overnight.

substeps.instruction: Dilute primary antibody to the desired working concentration (typically 2-20 µg/mL if company recommendations are unavailable) in Antibody Diluent Reagent during the blocking step.
Add diluted antibody to the section and incubate overnight at 4˚C.

steps.title: Wash and Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Wash sections and apply secondary antibodies if required.

substeps.instruction: Remove solution and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes, twice.
If primary antibody is directly conjugated with a fluorophore, skip to the Hoechst staining step.
If using indirect immunofluorescence, dilute fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody using Antibody Diluent Reagent.
Add antibody solution to sections and incubate for 60 minutes at room temperature.
Remove solution and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes, three times.

steps.title: Nuclear Staining and Mounting
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei with Hoechst and mount for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Incubate sections in Hoechst 33342 (1:5,000 dilution of 20mM solution in 1X PBS) for 10 minutes.
Remove Hoechst 33342 and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes, twice.
Mount slides in 50% glycerol in PBS; do not seal the coverslips.
Keep slides horizontal in a humidified chamber to prevent coverslips from falling off or sections from drying out.

steps.title: Imaging and Storage
steps.instruction: Image the slides and store them appropriately.

substeps.instruction: Image the slides.
Store slides at 4˚C in a moisture chamber.

steps.title: Coverslip Removal
steps.instruction: Remove the coverslip to prepare for the next cycle.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slides in a vertical staining jar filled with PBS for 30 minutes with slight agitation (e.g., plate rocker).
Slowly lift the slide from the vertical jar and allow the coverslip to release via gravity.
If the coverslip does not release, return the slide to PBS for an additional 15 minutes.
Wash slide in PBS for 5 minutes, three times to remove residual glycerol.
Place slides back in a vertical staining jar full of PBS with slight agitation to wash.

steps.title: Prepare Inactivation Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the sodium bicarbonate base and the final inactivation solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.5 M sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) by mixing 21 g of NaHCO3 with 500 ml ddH2O.
Adjust pH to 11.2 (acceptable range: 10.9-11.3) using sodium hydroxide pellets.
Store this solution at 4˚C for up to 6 months.
To prepare the inactivation solution (e.g., 10 ml), add 2 ml of 0.5 M NaHCO3 and 7 ml ddH2O to create a solution of 0.1 M NaHCO3, 3% H2O2 in ddH2O.
Aliquot the solution into five tubes (1.8 ml per tube).
Immediately prior to use, add 200 µl of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to each tube.

steps.title: Fluorophore Inactivation
steps.instruction: Inactivate fluorophores using the chemical solution and LED light.

substeps.instruction: Place slides on a plastic surface on top of an LED light system.
Add the fresh inactivation solution (containing H2O2) to each section.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes in the presence of white LED light.
Repeat this process with fresh solution four more times.
Remove solution and wash sections in PBS for 5 minutes, four times.

steps.title: Verification and Re-staining
steps.instruction: Verify inactivation and repeat nuclear staining for registration.

substeps.instruction: Mount slides in 50% glycerol and image to confirm complete fluorophore inactivation.
Remove the coverslip and wash three times for 5 minutes in PBS.
Place slides in a humidified chamber and cover sections in PBS using a pipettor to prevent drying.
Remove antibody solution (if applicable) and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes, three times.
Incubate sections in Hoechst (1:5,000 dilution in 1X PBS) for 5 minutes.
Remove Hoechst and wash sections with PBS for 5 minutes, twice.
Mount slides in 50% glycerol in PBS.
Image and store slides at 4˚C in a moisture chamber.
